feed.title: Java & JVM — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Ammonite
entry.summary: An advanced REPL that makes Scala usable for BASH-like filesystem operations.

entry.title: Awesome Scala
entry.summary: A topic-by-topic list of Scala libraries and tools. Unlike scattered search it shows functional and big-data libraries together.

entry.title: better-files
entry.summary: A thin NIO wrapper library that makes file operations in Scala easy. Unlike using java.nio directly, it reduces reading, writing and walking files to readable one-line Scala idioms.

entry.title: Clojure
entry.summary: A modern Lisp dialect on the JVM. Unlike Common Lisp, it uses Java libraries directly and its data structures are immutable by default.

entry.title: Coursier
entry.summary: A JVM dependency resolver and application launcher written in pure Scala. Unlike classic Maven/Ivy resolution it downloads in parallel and is much faster; sbt now resolves dependencies with it too.

entry.title: JCTools
entry.summary: Very high-performance concurrent queues for the JVM, used by projects like Netty. Unlike the java.util.concurrent queues, it offers lock-free designs specialised for single/multi producer–consumer cases.

entry.title: JMH
entry.summary: An OpenJDK tool for microbenchmarking on the JVM that accounts for JIT effects that distort measurement. Unlike timing by hand it correctly handles traps like warmup and dead-code elimination.

entry.title: Kotlin
entry.summary: A cross-platform language on the JVM, the preferred language for Android. Unlike Java it has null safety, a terser syntax and coroutines, while interoperating fully with Java code.

entry.title: OpenJDK
entry.summary: The open-source reference implementation of the Java platform — where the language and JVM are developed. Unlike vendor distributions the standard itself is defined here.

entry.title: Scala
entry.summary: A language on the JVM uniting object-oriented and functional programming — the language Spark is written in. Unlike Java it has strong type inference, pattern matching and functional collections.

entry.title: Scalastyle
entry.summary: A linter that checks Scala source against formatting and style rules; the project site is gone and the repository has been dormant since 2022. Unlike scalafmt it reports violations instead of reformatting; new projects mostly use Scalafix.

entry.title: Scoverage
entry.summary: A statement-based code-coverage tool for Scala, more precise than line-based coverage.

entry.title: Vavr
entry.summary: A library bringing persistent collections and functional control structures to Java. Unlike the standard collections it foregrounds immutability and types like Try/Either.

entry.title: Apache Maven
entry.summary: A tool doing dependency management and builds for Java with a standard project layout. Unlike collecting jars by hand it resolves dependencies from a central repository and defines a lifecycle.

entry.title: Awesome Java
entry.summary: A list organising Java libraries and frameworks by topic. Unlike a Maven Central search it is a curated, categorised and maintained starting map.

entry.title: Baeldung
entry.summary: The largest archive of worked, up-to-date tutorials for Java and Spring. Unlike the official docs it answers “how do I do this” with working code examples.

entry.title: Dev.java · Learn
entry.summary: Oracle’s current, official Java learning portal. Unlike the old Java Tutorials it is refreshed for modern versions and organised topic by topic.

entry.title: Gradle
entry.summary: A scriptable, incremental build tool for Java and Android. Unlike Maven’s XML it writes build logic in real code (Kotlin/Groovy) and rebuilds only what changed.

entry.title: Guava
entry.summary: Google’s core utility library for Java — collections, caching, functional extras. Unlike filling the standard library’s gaps by hand it closes them in a tested way.

entry.title: Hibernate
entry.summary: An ORM mapping Java objects to relational database rows. Unlike raw JDBC it largely abstracts the SQL and persists the object graph.

entry.title: Jackson
entry.summary: The de facto library for turning JSON into objects and back in Java. Unlike hand-written parsing it offers streaming, tree and data-binding modes under one roof.

entry.title: JUnit 5
entry.summary: Java’s standard unit-testing framework; the base of writing and running tests. Unlike trying things in main it brings assertions, lifecycle hooks and parameterised tests.

entry.title: Project Lombok
entry.summary: A tool that generates repetitive Java code like getters/setters and constructors from annotations at compile time. Unlike writing it by hand it keeps the class short and leaves the noise to the compiler.

entry.title: SDKMAN!
entry.summary: A command-line manager to install and switch between multiple versions of the JDK and JVM tools. Unlike editing PATH by hand it reduces per-project version switching to one command.

entry.title: Spring Boot
entry.summary: A framework that starts Spring applications running with no configuration burden. Unlike raw Spring it brings sensible defaults and an embedded server — “up with one command”.

entry.title: Spring Framework
entry.summary: The application framework that is the de facto standard for enterprise Java — dependency injection, web, data. Unlike stacking libraries it unifies them in one consistent model.

entry.title: The Java Tutorials
entry.summary: Oracle’s official Java tutorial, from language basics through collections and concurrency. Against third-party courses it explains the standard library’s intent first-hand; the price is a dry register and sections that stopped at older releases.
